findings.title: Windows predecessor recovery cannot restore the exact pair and trusts an unbound HEAD state
findings.reproduction: At exact reviewed-state commit 24185cc42b5da841a244d331b2c37bb51171ffd2 on the release-authoritative Windows worktree, SHA-256 of the CRLF planning/backlog.yaml worktree bytes is the approved BACKLOG_SHA256 0b3d22f30d3a024e37b6c7b9b07d48f3a0b96dd2fc6c1968809a21d35a2977e7, while SHA-256 of `git show HEAD:planning/backlog.yaml` is the normalized LF blob 17aa5c98e5146c61786cacb1f27e0c0189cd806e51f5a600f53b7b71448c7526. tools/gcr2ctl.py restore_predecessor reads the backlog and state with taskctl.git_blob(repo, current HEAD, path), then requires the backlog Git-blob hash to equal the CRLF worktree constant. In a disposable real-Git clone of the frozen branch, preserve the exact witness, commit an unrelated GCR-0002 state while leaving the backlog unchanged, replace the live state with partial-publication bytes, create only GCR-0002.B00.adoption.lock, and run `python tools/gcr2ctl.py --repo . recover GCR-0002 --agent codex`. The command exits 1 with `GCR-0002 predecessor backlog Git blob is not the approved revision-8 boundary`, leaves the lock present, and leaves the partial state in place instead of producing either exact terminal pair. Independently, restore_predecessor selects both records from whatever current HEAD happens to be; require_recovery_workspace does not bind HEAD to the adoption-evidence commit or bind the selected state blob to the approved predecessor. A naive line-ending-only fix would therefore permit an unrelated committed state to become the restored canonical state. The passing recovery tests mask the production condition by setting core.autocrlf=false and patching BACKLOG_SHA256 to the fixture worktree hash in both the missing-manifest and crash loops; the crash loop also patches validate_successor_pair. The declared evidence therefore does not establish criterion 8's exact Windows predecessor-or-successor recovery boundary.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant candidate, make missing, invalid, stale, and partial-manifest recovery authenticate and restore the exact raw predecessor backlog and state independently of an unbound current HEAD. Bind the recovery base to the exact adoption-evidence/approved-state authority, preserve or otherwise deterministically reproduce both raw preimages across the CRLF Git/worktree boundary, validate both raw and canonical hashes plus the strict state schema before publication, and reject unrelated or stale HEAD/state sources without cleanup or mutation. Add real-Git Windows CRLF tests that do not patch BACKLOG_SHA256 or successor validation and cover missing and invalid manifests, stale/unrelated HEAD, substituted state, every declared child-process interruption boundary, repeated recovery, durable cleanup, and byte-exact predecessor-or-successor terminal pairs. Preserve this R01 ledger append-only and submit fresh R02 evidence with an explicit closure for GCR-0002.B00-R01-F01.

findings.title: A self-consistent substituted review/evidence chain is accepted as predecessor authority
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate 28ee69a90e51be3d704a73371c1613ae3b7c91c3, validate_recovery_anchor requires the anchor HEAD to be a direct-child adoption-evidence commit and validates the parent state's schema, status, raw bytes, and canonical backlog, but it never proves that approvedStateCommit is the canonical independently approved GCR-0002.B00 review projection. It does not replay validate_history, bind the state's approval reference to the immutable GCR-0002 approval, require an approved latest attempt/ledger, or derive the exact ledger-introduction commit. In a disposable real-Git fixture, branch from the original approved-state parent, change only the schema-valid state approval sha256 and commit fields, commit that substituted APPROVED state, add a schema-valid adoption evidence file naming the substituted parent and commit it as the direct child, then create a self-consistent lock anchor whose state payload/binding names those bytes. With the exact witness present, replace the live backlog/state with partial bytes and call recover_transaction. The result is RESTORED_PREDECESSOR; the controller restores the unapproved state containing approval SHA ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff and removes every transaction artifact. The R02 test named `test_invalid_manifest_restores_but_stale_head_and_substituted_anchor_fail_closed` changes payload bytes under the original immutable commits or moves HEAD away from the anchor, so it does not cover a coherent substituted parent/evidence/anchor chain. This preserves the core R01 authority defect despite correcting CRLF raw-byte restoration and violates criterion 8's exact predecessor terminal-pair guarantee.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant candidate, authenticate approvedStateCommit as the unique canonical independently approved GCR-0002.B00 review projection before trusting any anchor preimage: validate the exact immutable approval reference; complete append-only submission/evidence/review history; latest independent approved ledger and absence of open blockers; exact reviewed-state-to-ledger/state projection delta; ledger/state Git blobs and hashes; and the exact adoption-evidence direct child. Recovery must reject a fully self-consistent alternate APPROVED parent/evidence/anchor chain, fork, altered approval reference, substituted ledger/history, or wrong candidate without changing backlog, state, lock, manifest, or successor artifacts. Add real-Git adversarial tests constructing those coherent alternate histories, preserve the Windows CRLF/unpatched crash tests, and submit fresh evidence that explicitly closes GCR-0002.B00-R02-F01.

closures.evidence: R02 fixes the literal Windows CRLF Git-blob mismatch by durably anchoring and restoring the raw backlog/state preimages; it binds HEAD to the anchor's evidence commit, rejects simple stale-HEAD and payload substitutions byte-stably, and removes the BACKLOG_SHA256 and successor-validation patches from focused crash recovery. The remaining authority part of R01-F01 is narrowed and reproduced as GCR-0002.B00-R02-F01: the anchor can substitute a complete schema-valid APPROVED parent plus matching direct-child evidence because that parent is not bound to the canonical independently approved review projection.

submission.rootCauseAnalysis: The first implementation trusted normalized Git blobs and test-patched validation instead of preserving the exact raw predecessor pair. R02 preserved raw bytes but authenticated structural self-consistency rather than deriving the one canonical human-approved, independently reviewed state, so a coherent alternate history could substitute its own authority. The shared root cause was piecemeal trust-boundary validation; R03 uses the existing append-only history and canonical approval-projection derivation as the sole anchor authority and tests substitution directly. The packet-level precursor was likewise caused by generic content bindings and runtime subobjects; distinct constant bindings and one strict runtime shape remain enforced.

findings.title: The canonical review projection trusts a ledger that contradicts its state record
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate e36f6f17193ff9a5615a77f8697e755529835eed, validate_history proves that each ledger path was introduced once in an exact two-file child commit and that its Git blob matches the hash recorded by the state, but it never parses or schema-validates that immutable ledger and never compares its reviewer, result, evidence, findings, or closures with the corresponding attempt projection in the state. canonical_approved_state then trusts only state.status, the state-side latest review result, the ledger Git blob equality, and the two-file commit shape. In a disposable real-Git fixture using the R03 controller, create the normal immutable approval, candidate, REVIEW submission, and direct-child review projection, but make the schema-valid immutable ledger result changes-requested with one blocking HIGH while making the state-side attempt result approved with no findings; record the exact adverse-ledger SHA-256 in the state. Both documents independently pass the v2 runtime schema, the projection changes exactly ledger plus state, and validate_history followed by canonical_approved_state accepts and derives that commit as canonical (`ADVERSE_LEDGER_ACCEPTED True`). The same unchecked boundary permits disagreement in findings, closures, evidence, reviewer, and notes. Recovery therefore can authenticate and restore a state that claims approval even though the unique immutable review document is adverse, contrary to the ordered-review authority required by R02-F01 and criterion 8.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant R04 candidate, make history validation load and v2-schema-validate every immutable ledger Git blob and require its complete review projection to match the corresponding state attempt: identity, attempt and candidate, reviewed-state commit, normalized independent reviewer, result, evidence, findings, closures, and notes. Reapply the controlled-review invariants to history: severity ordering and unique finding IDs, closures limited to the prior open set, exact open-finding evolution, and denial of approved whenever the ledger introduces any finding or any prior blocking finding remains unresolved. Derive canonical approval only from that reconciled latest ledger and state projection. Add real-Git tests for an adverse ledger paired with an approved state, an approved ledger paired with an adverse state, and individually substituted findings, closures, evidence, reviewer, and candidate; each recovery case must fail before changing or cleaning backlog, state, lock, manifest, or successor artifacts. Preserve the exact Windows CRLF predecessor restoration, unpatched successor validation, every child-process interruption boundary, immutable prior attempts, protected witness, and authorized scope, then submit fresh evidence explicitly closing this finding.

closures.evidence: R03 correctly binds the predecessor approval reference to the unique immutable GCR-0002 approval, replays the ordered Git introduction and exact two-file projection shape for each state-recorded review, requires the anchor to name the derived projection, preserves raw CRLF predecessor bytes, and rejects the R02 coherent altered-approval case byte-stably. The remaining authority defect is narrowed and reproduced as GCR-0002.B00-R03-F01: the ordered projection does not reconcile the immutable review document's adverse disposition and finding set with the state record that is used to derive approval.
